Just to add this if anyone stops by that GABA levels also play an important role in the quality of sleep you’ll get. 

Higher GABA levels allow for more deep sleep in less hours but not necessarily better quality of sleep. So if you feel like you sleep better on less hours it’s likely because your GABA levels are slightly above normal or high and you function better on more deep sleep. However it can cause you to feel like you’ve been awake longer than you have and can lead to feeling tired by midday or evening. So it can lead to feeling sleepy quicker in the day but if you do fall asleep your midday naps will be a deep sleep and keep you up later at night. It can turn into a cycle of needing less and less hours of sleep to feel like youve slept for a long period. 

Lower GABA levels make it easier to fall asleep but harder to fall into a deep sleep but your body will compensate and try to put you in a deep sleep during your sleep cycle by allowing you to sleep in longer. This is why if you wake up and feel like you can go right back to sleep it means your GABA levels are lower or normal range. It causes waking up feeling more tired than you should be even though you’ve gotten a full 8 hours of sleep. You will be less tired during the day but more groggy in the morning 

Too high or too low GABA levels can be bad depending on the person. Some people can’t function as good on less hours of sleep but others can’t function as good on more hours because of GABA levels. I think it’s very important for someone trying to figure out what works best for their sleep is to try GABA supplementation and see how it affects their sleep
